dedupe_keys.name: epal s wone leakage monitoring programme in lisbon climate adapt case study

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes WONE, the leakage monitoring programme that the Lisbon water company EPAL started in 2005 to cope with drought risk and conserve water. A monitoring system and purpose-built software compare expected with real-time water use in the distribution network, flag discrepancies traced back to the meters that show them, and send leak detection teams to find and repair the leak. EPAL spent about 1 million euros on the software and a similar sum on monitoring, and runs the programme for about 500,000 euros a year; non-revenue water fell from 23.5 per cent in 2005 to about 8.5 per cent in 2015, saving about 68 million euros over ten years. Coverage is EPAL's Lisbon distribution network. The page is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal, published in 2023 and updated in 2026. Caveats: the figures come from the utility, and the software itself is not published. Simulation uses: leakage reduction targets and costs for drought resilience of water networks. Related records: the BattLeDIM leakage benchmark (data-battledim-leakage-detection-benchmark) and LeakDB (data-leakdb).
